body:
# Independent audit: John contacts of balanced source moment bodies

Audited `candidate 0ca1f875b898090e`, Sections1–6, and ran
`supporting computation verify_john_contact_balanced_moment_duals.py` successfully. Result: PASS under
the displayed ordinary-volume normalization.

The minimal-base-face reduction is valid because every face of the finite
base polytope is exposed. Strictly positive balanced base coefficients exist
at its relative-interior point j; mixing a sufficiently small strictly
fractional source with a maximum-mass source produces a uniformly fractional
source at every `0<t<T`. This gives the stated coercive lower bound in the
quotient parameter space. Nonzero continuous direction makes all cap
boundaries null on each positive fiber, so ordinary differentiation yields
exact mass and base balance. Extending a face dual by an exposing base
functional excludes every other fiber. Equality in the positive-part dual
proves uniqueness of the entire maximizing source, not necessarily uniqueness
of its dual parameter pair.

The contact cone is closed by its fixed positive trace. Separation and a
uniformly strict first-order ellipsoid perturbation prove the John equations
without assuming an unproved normal balance. The contact-source centroid
identity then follows from uniqueness of the support point. The normalized
mixture is indeed dominated: its coefficient weights sum to one. Both its
mean and covariance are exactly as displayed.

The hinge signs in (6)–(8) are correct. Testing the remaining integer affine
function on a maximum balanced source gives `-BT` regardless of B's sign,
so `B>=-dt/(T-t)` and the stated upper bound follow. There is no cancellation
of the integer aggregate. The rational three-interval example verifies
regularity and local strict convexity of both support duals, their uniqueness,
the surviving integer coefficient, the hinge values, and the distinct bad
ambient tilt through the John center.

Section6 also checks. Scaling a dominated source proves nesting. The
homothetic single-fiber sources give explicit Hausdorff convergence to K_j.
A represented point on its boundary would force a positive source onto an
ambient support plane with nonzero continuous component, a null set for the
mixed measure. Compact strict inclusion permits a small dilation and proves
strict John-volume loss at every positive mass; it is not merely an inference
from set inequality.

One wording correction was sent to the author: if the optional common factor
`c dx` is used, define `w_z=mu({z}xK_z)=c|K_z|` as the capacity. In Section6
use this same w in `theta=(s/w)^(1/d)`. The literal `w=|K_j|` formula applies
to the displayed main case `c=1`.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
